§ 2Why this matters for SSC

National Symbols questions are 1–2 markers and freebies once memorized. Adopted the Bharat name alongside India in 2023 (Article 1) — keep that in mind.

§ 3Comprehensive list of National Symbols

SymbolNameKey facts
National FlagTirangaThree horizontal stripes — saffron (courage, top), white (peace, middle) with 24-spoke Ashoka Chakra (navy blue, Dharma), green (faith, bottom). Designed by Pingali Venkayya. Adopted on 22 July 1947. The Chakra's 24 spokes represent the 24 hours of a day.
National EmblemState Emblem of IndiaAdopted 26 January 1950. Adapted from the Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath (c. 250 BC). Three lions visible (one hidden), four Asiatic lions total. The motto "Satyameva Jayate" ("Truth Alone Triumphs") is inscribed below, from Mundaka Upanishad. The words read top-to-bottom, not left-to-right.
National AnthemJana Gana ManaWritten by Rabindranath Tagore. Adopted 24 January 1950. Composed originally in Bengali as Bharat Bhagya Vidhata. First sung at Calcutta session of INC on 27 December 1911. Playing time ≈ 52 seconds.
National SongVande MataramWritten by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay (in Anandamath, 1882). Adopted in Hindi version. Has the same status as the anthem but is not played on official occasions.
National CalendarSaka CalendarAdopted on 22 March 1957 by the Calendar Reform Committee. Chaitra is the first month (Chaitra 1 = 22 March, normally).
National AnimalRoyal Bengal TigerAdopted in 1973, the year of Project Tiger. Scientific name: Panthera tigris.
National BirdIndian PeacockAdopted 1963. Scientific name: Pavo cristatus.
National FlowerLotusAdopted 1950. Scientific name: Nelumbo nucifera.
National TreeBanyan TreeAdopted 1950. Scientific name: Ficus benghalensis. National tree of India, also of Bangladesh.
National FruitMangoAdopted 1950. Scientific name: Mangifera indica.
National VegetablePumpkin (Kaddu)Adopted 2021. (Recently added)
National RiverGangaAdopted 2008 (declared by PM, not by any statute).
National Game(No official national game)There is NO official national game of India — hockey is often wrongly claimed. The RTI reply by the Government in 2012 confirmed this.
National ReptileKing CobraAdopted 2021 (Snake Awareness Day). Scientific name: Ophiophagus hannah.
National Aquatic AnimalGanges River DolphinAdopted 2011 (declared by PM on 5 Oct, Ganga River Dolphin Day).
National Heritage AnimalIndian ElephantAdopted 2010.
National Insect(No official national insect yet)Common contenders: Papilionidae (swallowtail butterfly) and ladybird beetle.
National Bird (additional)Indian Roller — state bird of several states.(See [[02 - Folk Dances of IndiaFolk Dances]] for related cultural items.)
National Pledge"India is my country…"Written by Pydimarri Venkata Subba Rao (Telugu), adopted 1968. Originally composed in Telugu.
National War MemorialNational War Memorial, New DelhiInaugurated 25 February 2019 (named Amar Jawan Jyoti was shifted to it). 16 February 2021 — 50th anniversary of Vijay Diwas — etc.
National War Memorial NoteIndia Gate (New Delhi) — built 1921, designed by Edwin LutyensMemorial to 84,000 Indian soldiers of WWI.
National MottoSatyameva JayateAdopted 26 January 1950. From Mundaka Upanishad (last line, 3.1.6).
National Emblem of the flagAshoka Chakra24-spoke navy-blue wheel from the Lion Capital of Ashoka. Diameter: ratio 3/4 of the white band.
National MicroorganismLactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus(Often cited in older books; not currently in use.)

§ 4State Emblem – what is shown and what's NOT

  • Three lions standing back-to-back (mounted on a circular abacus). A fourth lion is hidden from view (on the other side).
  • Abacus (base): a horse, a bull, an elephant, and a lion — separated by smaller wheels (chakras) over an inverted lotus.
  • The motto "Satyameva Jayate" is inscribed below.
  • NOT the words "Government of India" — those are in the letterhead, not the emblem.
  • The phrase "Satyameva Jayate" also appears on the Indian rupee note and the National Emblem.

§ 5Jana Gana Mana — quick facts

  • Written by Rabindranath Tagore in Bengali.
  • First published in Tatwabodhini Patrika, 5 November 1912.
  • The Constituent Assembly adopted the full song as the anthem on 24 January 1950 (not 26 Jan).
  • Both India and Bangladesh have Tagore-composed national anthems, but they are different songs: India's is "Jana Gana Mana"; Bangladesh's is "Amar Sonar Bangla" (My Golden Bengal).
  • The 2nd and 3rd stanzas are not part of the official anthem.
  • It is played for 52 seconds; when played in full, 1 min 5 sec.

§ 6Vande Mataram — quick facts

  • Composed in Sanskrit by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay in 1876.
  • Published in Anandamath (1882).
  • The first two stanzas are the national song; the rest are literary content.
  • Sung at the 1896 INC session for the first time by Rabindranath Tagore.

§ 7The Tiranga — dimensions and code

  • Aspect ratio: 3:2 (width to length).
  • Top saffron band represents courage and sacrifice.
  • White middle band represents peace and truth; bears the Ashoka Chakra.
  • Bottom green band represents faith and chivalry.
  • The Chakra's 24 spokes stand for the 24 hours of the day; the wheel itself is the Wheel of Law (Dharma Chakra) from the Sarnath pillar.

§ 8Trivia (often asked in SSC)

  • Rajya Sabha adopted Vande Mataram as the national song; Jana Gana Mana is for the Lok Sabha & State Legislatures also.
  • Satyameva Jayate is NOT the national motto of India in the sense of being statutory — it is the motto inscribed under the State Emblem. (Sometimes books list it as the motto — both are acceptable in SSC.)
  • The phrase "Satyameva Jayate" — the first time it was used in a non-scriptural context was in B.R. Ambedkar's writings.
  • India's name was changed to "Bharat" — there is no formal legal change; Article 1 of the Constitution says "India, that is Bharat". In 2023 the G20 invite used "President of Bharat" (under India's presidency) — used alongside India.
  • National Voters Day is celebrated on 25 January (founders' day of ECI — Election Commission of India).
  • Indian Post Independence Day for the National Flag is celebrated on Swachh Bharat Diwas etc. The official Flag Code was updated 2022, allowing machine-made flags and the general public to fly the flag on any day, with decorum.

§ 9Quick recall for exam

  • Emblem → Lion Capital of Ashoka (Sarnath).
  • Flag → Designed by Pingali Venkayya.
  • Anthem → Tagore; song of 52 seconds; first sang 1911.
  • Song → Bankim; Sanskrit.
  • Calendar → Saka.
  • Animal → Tiger (Project Tiger, 1973).
  • Bird → Peacock (1963).
  • Flower → Lotus.
  • Tree → Banyan.
  • Fruit → Mango; Vegetable → Pumpkin (2021).
  • Game → No official national game (hockey is not the national game).
  • River → Ganga.
  • Reptile → King Cobra (2021).
  • Aquatic animal → Gangetic Dolphin.
  • Heritage animal → Indian Elephant (2010).

§ 10Key concepts

  • State Emblem of India (Lion Capital of Ashoka) — adopted 26 Jan 1950.
  • Jana Gana Mana — Tagore, 1911/1950.
  • Tiranga — 3:2 ratio, 24-spoke Ashoka Chakra.
  • Vande Mataram — Bankim Chandra, 1882.
  • No official national game of India.
  • Ashoka Chakra is taken from the Sarnath Pillar of Ashoka.

§ 112024–2025 Updates

  • Bharat vs India (Article 1): In 2023, the G20 invites used "President of Bharat" instead of "President of India" — re-ignited the long-running debate. In 2024, several Union Ministers, official communiqués, and even the ICHR started using "Bharat" more frequently; some states (e.g., Tamil Nadu) passed resolutions to keep "India" as well. For SSC: Article 1 — "India, that is Bharat" — both names are constitutionally valid.
  • High Court ruling on National Anthem (Kerala, 2024): A Kerala HC division bench in Jan 2024 held that the National Anthem need not be played in every cinema hall before every film show (a 2016 direction of the SC was already partially relaxed by the SC itself in 2018). For SSC: the anthem remains Jana Gana Mana; no change in status.
  • New Parliament Building (inaugurated 28 May 2023 by PM Modi) — houses the Constitution Hall, Sengol placed near the Speaker's chair. For SSC: still part of the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha premises; not a separate national symbol.
  • Sengol (a Chola-era royal scepter) installed near the Speaker's chair in the new Parliament (2023) — a reminder of the transfer-of-power ceremony at Independence.
  • National Symbols unchanged in 2024–25: Flag, Anthem, Song, Emblem, Calendar, Animal, Bird, Flower, Tree, Fruit, River, Game, Reptile, Aquatic Animal — all retain their 1950–2021 adoptions.
No new national symbol was added in 2024–25. Memorize the canonical list (above table).
